docs.title: Servers Overview
docs.text: RingCentral currently publishes two MCP servers. Both implement the Model Context Protocol specification and are reachable over HTTPS using Server-Sent Events (SSE) transport.

docs.title: Server registry
docs.text: Server URL Status Tools RingCentral MCP https://mcp.labs.ringcentral.com 🟡 Labs / Beta — App Connect https://unified-crm-extension.labs.ringcentral.com/mcp 🟢 Available 9

docs.title: Transport & protocol
docs.text:
Both servers use SSE (Server-Sent Events) transport over HTTPS, which is the recommended transport for remote MCP servers. Clients connect by sending an HTTP POST to the server URL with a JSON-RPC 2.0 body.

# Discover tools on any server
curl -X POST https://<server-url> \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list","params":{}}'

docs.title: Authentication model
docs.text:
• RingCentral MCP — no authentication required for tool discovery; some tools may require a valid RingCentral session.
  • App Connect — tools marked ⚠️ REQUIRES CRM CONNECTION require the user to have authenticated with both RingCentral and a supported CRM platform.

docs.title: Versioning policy
docs.text: Labs servers follow a rolling-release model. Breaking changes will be announced in the Changelog with at least 14 days notice. Stable tools are versioned via api-version query parameter where applicable.

docs.title: About
docs.text:
The App Connect MCP server bridges RingCentral telephony with your connected CRM platform. It enables AI assistants to look up contacts, create CRM records, and sync call activity — all through natural language.

Supported CRM platforms include Salesforce, HubSpot, Zoho, and others supported by the RingCentral App Connect product.

docs.title: Connecting
Authentication
docs.text:
This server uses a two-layer auth model:

  1. RingCentral identity — required for all tools. Uses OAuth 2.0 / SSO via your RingCentral account.
  2. CRM connection — required for tools marked ⚠️ REQUIRES CRM CONNECTION. Users must link their CRM account via the App Connect portal.

See the Setup guide for step-by-step connection instructions.

docs.title: About
docs.text:
The RingCentral MCP server gives your AI assistant direct access to the RingCentral platform. Read call logs, search the company directory, send and read team messages, retrieve voicemails and SMS, and pull AI-generated call notes — all through natural language.

Run platform_get_capabilities to see a full summary of supported API endpoints and tools.

Labs status

This server is part of RingCentral Labs and is not covered by RingCentral's standard SLA. Tools may be renamed, modified, or removed without prior notice. Use in production environments with caution.

docs.title: Connect to ChatGPT
docs.text:
ChatGPT supports remote MCP servers through its Connectors feature. Once connected, you can invoke RingCentral tools directly in your conversations.

Subscription required

ChatGPT Connectors require a Pro, Team, Enterprise, or Edu subscription. The feature is not available on the free tier.

docs.title: Server URLs
docs.text: Server URL App Connect https://unified-crm-extension.labs.ringcentral.com/mcp RingCentral MCP https://mcp.labs.ringcentral.com/ringex

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Step 1 — Enable Developer ModeStep 2 — Create a connectorStep 3 — AuthenticateStep 4 — Enable for a conversation

ChatGPT Connectors require Developer Mode to be enabled:

  1. Sign in to chatgpt.com
  2. Click your profile picture (top right) → Settings
  3. Navigate to Connectors
  4. Click Advanced at the bottom of the page
  5. Toggle Developer mode on
  1. In Settings → Connectors, click Create connector

  2. Enter the server URL in the Base URL field:

    https://unified-crm-extension.labs.ringcentral.com/mcp

  3. Give it a name, e.g. RingCentral App Connect

  4. Click Save

Repeat to add the RingCentral MCP server if needed:

https://mcp.labs.ringcentral.com/ringex

After saving, ChatGPT will initiate the RingCentral OAuth flow:

  1. A browser window will open asking you to sign in to RingCentral
  2. Authorize the integration
  3. You will be redirected back to ChatGPT

Connectors must be explicitly enabled for each conversation:

  1. Open a new chat
  2. Click the + icon in the message compose area
  3. Select More → find your RingCentral connector
  4. Toggle it on

The connector is now active for that conversation.

docs.title: Connect your CRM
docs.text:
Once the App Connect server is active in a conversation, link your CRM:

  1. Ask: "What CRM platforms can I connect?"
  2. ChatGPT will display available connectors
  3. Follow the OAuth flow to link your CRM account

docs.title: Using tools in a conversation
docs.text:
With the connector enabled, invoke tools through natural language:

Check my RingCentral session status.

Look up the contact for +1 415 555 0123 in my CRM.

Show me my call logs from today and log the most recent one to Salesforce.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Connector not appearing in the + menu

  • Confirm Developer Mode is enabled in Settings → Connectors → Advanced
  • Verify the connector was saved successfully in Settings → Connectors

Authentication errors

  • Delete the connector and re-create it to restart the OAuth flow
  • Ensure your RingCentral account has the necessary API permissions

Tools returning CRM errors

  • Ask: "What is my session status?" — if crmConnected is false, re-link your CRM by asking "What CRM platforms can I connect?"

Connector scope per conversation

Connectors are enabled per-conversation, not globally. You need to activate the connector each time you start a new chat where you want to use RingCentral tools.

docs.title: Adding a local stdio server
docs.text:
If you need to add a local MCP server (one that runs as a process on your machine), you can use claude_desktop_config.json:

OS Path macOS ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json Windows %APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json Linux ~/.config/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json 
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "my-local-server": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "my-mcp-package"]
    }
  }
}

Restart Claude Desktop after saving.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Tools not appearing after connecting

  • Confirm the URL has no trailing slash
  • Disconnect and reconnect the server from Settings → Connectors
  • Check that your network allows outbound HTTPS to *.ringcentral.com and *.labs.ringcentral.com

Authentication errors

  • Go to Settings → Connectors → disconnect and reconnect
  • Ensure your RingCentral account has the necessary API permissions

CRM tools returning errors

  • Ask: "What is my session status?" — if crmConnected is false, re-link your CRM
  • Re-authenticate via Settings → Connectors — disconnect and reconnect the server

docs.title: Connect to Codex
docs.text: The Codex app supports remote MCP servers through its MCP Servers settings. Once connected and authenticated, RingCentral tools are available in your Codex sessions.

docs.title: Server URLs
docs.text: Server URL RingCentral MCP https://mcp.labs.ringcentral.com/ringex

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Step 1 — Open MCP ServersStep 2 — Add the serverStep 3 — AuthenticateStep 4 — Verify
  1. Open the Codex app
  2. Click Settings (bottom left) → Settings
  3. Navigate to MCP Servers
  4. Click Add server

Fill in the server details and click Save:

Field Value Name RingCentral MCP (any name works) Type Streamable HTTP URL https://mcp.labs.ringcentral.com/ringex

After saving, Codex returns you to the MCP server list automatically.

  1. Click Authenticate on the server you just added
  2. Sign in with your RingCentral account in the browser window that opens
  3. Authorize the integration

In a new session, ask:

Using RingCentral, show my extension profile.

You should see your RingCentral extension details returned.

docs.title: Telling Codex to use RingCentral tools
docs.text:
Unlike ChatGPT or Claude, Codex has no picker to nominate a specific MCP tool for a conversation. Codex infers which of its enabled MCP servers to use from your prompt alone.

Mention RingCentral explicitly so Codex picks the right tools:

Using RingCentral, show me my call logs from today.

This is a RingCentral task — list my team messaging chats.

If Codex keeps reaching for other tools, add more context (e.g. "use the RingCentral MCP server") or temporarily disable other MCP servers in Settings → MCP Servers.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Server changes not taking effect

  • Codex can get stuck and fail to refresh its MCP configuration after you add or edit a server. Close and re-open the Codex app to force a refresh.

Codex not using RingCentral tools

  • Mention RingCentral explicitly in your prompt — Codex selects tools by inference, not by attachment
  • Temporarily disable other MCP servers to reduce ambiguity

Authentication errors

  • Re-run Authenticate from the MCP server list
  • Remove the server, re-add it, and authenticate again to restart the OAuth flow
  • Ensure your RingCentral account has the necessary API permissions

docs.title: Coaching & Insights
docs.text: Use AI to analyze your communication patterns, surface areas for improvement, and benchmark your outcomes against your own history — all grounded in real call data.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: When your AI has access to your full call history and transcripts, it can act as a communication coach rather than just a note-taker. It can identify patterns across dozens or hundreds of calls: which conversations lead to outcomes, how long your calls typically run, how often you follow up, and where your pacing or messaging could be sharper.

docs.title: Sales call pattern analysis
docs.text:
Review my last 20 outbound sales calls. What patterns come up in the ones that ended with a scheduled follow-up? AI

Analyzed 20 outbound calls from the past 6 weeks. Of the 8 that converted to a follow-up:

  • Average duration was 2.3× longer (14 min vs 6 min)
  • You asked an open-ended question in the first 90 seconds
  • Discovery covered budget, timeline, and decision process

In calls without follow-ups, conversations focused on features before understanding the buyer's situation.

Want specific examples of the opening questions that worked best?

docs.title: Objection frequency
docs.text:
What objections am I hearing most in my calls this month? AI

From 34 call transcripts in May, the top objections were:

  • "We already have a solution" — 12 mentions
  • "Not the right time / budget" — 9 mentions
  • "Need to involve my manager" — 7 mentions

In 4 of the "not the right time" calls you moved to a follow-up. You have no recorded recovery strategy for the "already have a solution" objection.

Want me to suggest some approaches based on what's worked in similar calls?

docs.title: Topic flagging across calls
docs.text:
Flag any calls in the last two weeks where the customer mentioned pricing, cancellation, or a competitor by name. AI

Found 6 calls matching those topics (Apr 28 – May 12):

  • Pricing mentioned: 4 calls — Brightpath (May 2), Vertex Inc. (May 5), two others
  • Competitor named: 2 calls — "Zoom Phone" came up in both
  • Cancellation: 0 mentions

Want me to pull the transcript excerpts where these topics came up?

docs.title: Tools called
docs.text: Step Tool Description 1 rcGetCallLogs Retrieve call records and transcripts for the target period 2 (AI synthesis) Pattern analysis, theme extraction, and coaching recommendations

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• RingCentral MCP server connected to your AI client
  • RingSense AI or call recording enabled to generate transcripts
  • Sufficient call history for meaningful analysis (10+ calls recommended)

Better results with transcripts

Coaching insights are significantly richer when transcript data is available. Without transcripts, analysis is limited to metadata like duration, direction, and time of day.

docs.title: Communication Analytics
docs.text: Turn your call history into actionable intelligence. Query call volume trends, duration patterns, busiest hours, and transcript content — without building a report or writing a query.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: RingCentral stores a complete log of every call made across your organization. The RingCentral MCP server exposes that data to your AI, which can slice it any way you ask — by time range, direction, extension, or contact — and surface patterns that would take hours to find manually.

Last call: April 29 — you discussed moving to an annual plan. No decision recorded yet.

docs.title: CRM Enrichment
docs.text: Automate CRM hygiene through natural language. Log calls, capture leads, look up contacts, and attach conversation notes — without ever leaving your AI client.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: After a sales call or customer conversation, keeping your CRM up to date is tedious but critical. With App Connect, your AI can handle the entire post-call workflow: finding the right contact record, logging the call with duration and notes, and creating a new lead if no record exists — all from a single prompt.

  • Note added: Evaluating enterprise plan, demo requested
  • Logged: today at 2:14 PM

I didn't find an open opportunity for this account. Want me to create one?

Your AI can place outbound calls, send SMS messages, read incoming texts, and surface unheard voicemails — enabling fully conversational customer engagement workflows without switching between apps.

docs.title: Meetings Intelligence
docs.text: Stop losing track of what was decided, who owns what, and what was promised. Let AI search your meeting history, extract to-dos, and keep you accountable across every recorded session.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: RingCentral stores recordings, transcripts, and AI summaries for every RingCentral Video meeting. The MCP server makes that archive searchable and actionable — your AI can find past meetings by topic or participant, extract decisions and action items from a specific session, and surface anything that's gone unresolved.

Transcript quality

Action item and decision extraction works best with full transcripts. AI summaries alone may miss nuance — if precision matters, enable full transcript capture in your RingCentral Video settings.

docs.title: Team Collaboration
docs.text: Search your team's message history, send messages to channels or direct conversations, and maintain full context across your internal communications — without leaving your AI client.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: RingCentral Team Messaging stores the full history of every direct message and group conversation in your organization. The MCP server makes that history available to your AI, which can search across channels, surface relevant threads, and send new messages on your behalf — keeping you in the loop without constant context-switching.

docs.title: Catch up on a channel thread
docs.text:
What did the engineering team discuss about the rate limit issue in #platform-eng this week? AI

Here's what was shared in #platform-eng this week about rate limits:

  • Tuesday: Diego flagged that 3 enterprise customers hit the 1,000 req/min ceiling. Kevin confirmed it's a known limitation. No ticket opened yet.
  • Wednesday: Mei shared a proposed fix — tiered limits by plan. Thread got 7 reactions but no decision recorded.

No resolution reached. Want me to draft a message asking for a decision, or create a Jira ticket?

docs.title: Send a channel message
docs.text:
Send a message to the #releases channel: "v2.4.1 is live. Changelog is in the docs." AI

Message posted to #releases:

"v2.4.1 is live. Changelog is in the docs."

Sent at 3:12 PM. 4 team members are currently active in that channel.

docs.title: Cross-channel search
docs.text:
Has anyone mentioned the Apex Group deal in any channel in the last two weeks? AI

Found 6 mentions of Apex Group across 3 channels (Apr 28 – May 12):

  • #sales (3 mentions): Tyler noted they're in legal review. Bonnie asked if they need a custom SLA.
  • #exec-updates (2 mentions): Deal flagged as high-priority in weekly update.
  • #customer-success (1 mention): Onboarding plan drafted but not shared with Apex yet.

Bonnie's custom SLA question hasn't been answered. Want me to surface that thread?

docs.title: Tools called
docs.text: Step Tool Description 1 (Message search) Search team chat history by keyword, channel, or participant 2 (Message read) Retrieve a specific thread or conversation 3 (Message send) Post a new message to a channel or direct conversation

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• RingCentral MCP server connected to your AI client
  • Active RingCentral account with Team Messaging enabled
  • Appropriate permissions to read and post in the target channels

Sending messages requires confirmation

Like all write actions, sending a team message is irreversible. Your AI client will typically ask for your approval before posting on your behalf.

docs.title: createCallLog
docs.text:
Creates a single call activity log in the connected CRM platform. Can accept a raw RingCentral call log record (from rcGetCallLogs) or manually supplied fields.

Server: App Connect CRM required: ⚠️ Yes

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Required Description incomingData object — A complete RingCentral call log record. Pass items from rcGetCallLogs directly here — no field mapping needed. contactId string — CRM contact ID to associate the log with. contactType string — Type of the CRM contact object (e.g. "Contact", "Lead"). Required by some CRMs when contactId is set. note string — Free-text note or call summary to attach to the log entry.

At least one parameter recommended

All parameters are technically optional, but a useful log entry typically needs at least incomingData or contactId + note.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: Field Type Description logId string ID of the created CRM activity record crmUrl string \| null Deep link to the log entry in the CRM UI

docs.title: Example
Recommended workflow
docs.text:
The most complete log entry combines data from rcGetCallLogs with a contact lookup and a human-written note:

1. rcGetCallLogs       → get raw call record
2. findContactByPhone  → resolve CRM contact ID
3. createCallLog       → post log with incomingData + contactId + note

One log per call

This tool creates one log entry per invocation. To log multiple calls, call it once per record from rcGetCallLogs.

CRM connection required

This tool will return an authentication error if no CRM is connected.

docs.title: createContact
docs.text:
Creates a new contact record in the connected CRM platform. Returns the newly created contact's CRM ID and details.

Server: App Connect CRM required: ⚠️ Yes

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description phoneNumber string ✅ Phone number in E.164 format, e.g. +14155551234 newContactName string — Full name of the new contact. If omitted, the contact is created with only a phone number.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
The created contact object:

Field Type Description id string CRM record ID of the new contact name string \| null Name as stored in the CRM phone string Phone number as stored crmUrl string Deep link to the new record in the CRM UI

docs.title: Example
Notes
docs.text:
• The phoneNumber field must be in E.164 format. Use + followed by country code and number, no spaces or dashes.
  • Duplicate detection is handled by the CRM platform. If a contact with that phone number already exists, the CRM may return an error or the existing record depending on your CRM's settings.
  • After creating a contact, the returned id can be passed directly to createCallLog.

CRM connection required

This tool will return an authentication error if no CRM is connected.

Related tools

  • findContactByPhone — check for existing contacts before creating
  • createCallLog — immediately log a call against the new contact

docs.title: findContactByName
docs.text:
Searches the connected CRM for contacts whose name matches the provided string. Returns contact details including phone numbers, email, and CRM record IDs.

Server: App Connect CRM required: ⚠️ Yes

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description name string ✅ Full or partial name to search for (e.g. "Jane", "Jane Smith")

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
An array of matching contact objects:

Field Type Description id string CRM record ID name string Full name phone string \| null Primary phone number email string \| null Primary email address company string \| null Associated company or account name crmUrl string \| null Deep link to the record in the CRM UI

Returns an empty array [] if no matches are found.

docs.title: Example
Notes
docs.text:
• Search is case-insensitive and supports partial matches.
  • If multiple contacts match, all are returned. The AI client is responsible for disambiguation.
  • Use the returned id as the contactId parameter when calling createCallLog.

CRM connection required

This tool will return an authentication error if no CRM is connected. Call getSessionInfo first to verify.

Related tools

  • findContactByPhone — search by phone number instead
  • createContact — create a contact if none is found
  • createCallLog — log a call against the found contact

docs.title: findContactByPhone
docs.text:
Searches the connected CRM for a contact matching the given phone number. Ideal for automatic caller lookup when an inbound call arrives.

Server: App Connect CRM required: ⚠️ Yes

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description phoneNumber string ✅ Phone number to search for. Accepts E.164 format (+14155550123) or local formats — the server normalises before searching.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
An array of matching contact objects (same schema as findContactByName):

Field Type Description id string CRM record ID name string Full name phone string \| null Primary phone number email string \| null Primary email address company string \| null Associated company or account name crmUrl string \| null Deep link to the CRM record

Returns an empty array [] if no match is found.

docs.title: Example
Notes
docs.text:
• Phone number normalisation handles common formats: (415) 555-0123, 415-555-0123, +1 415 555 0123.
  • When no contact is found, consider calling createContact to add them.

CRM connection required

This tool will return an authentication error if no CRM is connected.

Common workflow

Inbound call → findContactByPhone → display contact info → after call ends → createCallLog

docs.title: getHelp
docs.text:
Returns a quick-start guide describing what the App Connect integration can do and how to get started. Useful as an onboarding prompt when a user first connects the server to their AI client.

Server: App Connect CRM required: No

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: This tool takes no parameters.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
A plain-text or markdown guide covering:

  • What App Connect does
  • How to authenticate with a CRM
  • A summary of available tools and common workflows

docs.title: Example
Notes
docs.text:
• This tool is safe to call before authentication is complete.
  • Intended for use at session start or when a user asks "what can you do?"

Related tools

  • getSessionInfo — check current auth status
  • getPublicConnectors — list connectable CRMs

docs.title: getPublicConnectors
docs.text:
Returns the list of CRM connectors publicly available through App Connect. Use this to show users which CRM platforms they can link to their RingCentral account.

Server: App Connect CRM required: No

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: This tool takes no parameters.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
An array of connector objects:

Field Type Description id string Unique connector identifier name string Human-readable CRM platform name logoUrl string URL to the connector's logo image authType string Authentication method ("oauth2", "apikey", etc.) status string Availability status ("available", "beta", "deprecated")

docs.title: Example
getSessionInfo
docs.text:
Returns the current user's RingCentral identity and their CRM connection status. Use this tool to verify a session is active before calling tools that require CRM authentication.

Server: App Connect CRM required: No

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: This tool takes no parameters.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
A session object containing:

Field Type Description rcUserId string RingCentral user ID rcUserName string Display name of the authenticated RC user rcExtension string RC extension number crmConnected boolean Whether a CRM platform is linked crmPlatform string \| null Name of the connected CRM (e.g. "Salesforce") crmUserId string \| null User ID in the CRM system

docs.title: Example
Notes
docs.text:
• If crmConnected is false, calls to CRM-dependent tools will return an authentication error.
  • Use this as a health-check at the start of automated workflows.

Related tools

  • getPublicConnectors — see which CRM platforms are available to connect
  • logout — end the CRM session

docs.title: logout
docs.text:
Signs the current user out of the connected CRM platform. The RingCentral session remains active; only the CRM link is severed.

Server: App Connect CRM required: No

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: This tool takes no parameters.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
A confirmation object:

Field Type Description success boolean true if the CRM session was successfully terminated message string Human-readable status message

docs.title: Example
Notes
docs.text:
• After calling logout, tools that require CRM authentication will return an error until the user reconnects.
  • To reconnect, the user must re-authenticate via the App Connect portal or the AI client's integration settings.
  • This does not log the user out of RingCentral itself.

Related tools

  • getSessionInfo — confirm logout was successful

docs.title: rcGetCallLogs
docs.text:
Fetches call log records from the RingCentral platform for the authenticated user within a specified time range. Records can be passed directly to createCallLog without field mapping.

Server: App Connect CRM required: ⚠️ Yes

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description timeFrom string ✅ Start of the time range in ISO 8601 format, e.g. 2025-05-01T00:00:00Z timeTo string ✅ End of the time range in ISO 8601 format, e.g. 2025-05-06T23:59:59Z

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
An object containing a records array. Each record is a complete RingCentral call log object:

Field Type Description id string Unique call log ID sessionId string Session ID (groups legs of the same call) startTime string ISO 8601 timestamp when the call started duration number Call duration in seconds type string "Voice", "Fax", etc. direction string "Inbound" or "Outbound" result string "Accepted", "Missed", "Voicemail", etc. from object Caller info: { phoneNumber, name, extensionNumber } to object Callee info: { phoneNumber, name, extensionNumber } recording object \| null Recording metadata if available

docs.title: Example
Passing records to createCallLog
docs.text:
Each item in records[] can be passed directly as incomingData.logInfo to createCallLog — no field renaming required:

// Use records[0] directly
{
  "name": "createCallLog",
  "arguments": {
    "incomingData": { "logInfo": <records[0]> },
    "contactId": "0031g00000XxYyZAAZ",
    "note": "Call summary here"
  }
}

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Maximum date range is 7 days per request. For longer ranges, make multiple calls with sequential windows.
  • Results are ordered by startTime descending (most recent first).
  • Calls from all devices and extensions under the authenticated account are included.

CRM connection required

This tool requires an active RingCentral session. The user must be authenticated via RingCentral OAuth.

Related tools

  • createCallLog — write fetched records to your CRM
  • findContactByPhone — resolve caller identity from from.phoneNumber

docs.title: RingCentral MCP Tools
docs.text:
Tools provided by the RingCentral MCP server (https://mcp.labs.ringcentral.com/ringex). This server exposes 23 tools covering team messaging, call log, messages, directory search, presence, extension management, and AI-generated call notes.

CRM required: No — all tools operate against the authenticated user's RingCentral account directly.

docs.title: Meta & discovery
docs.text:
Tools for understanding what the server can do and routing user requests to the right tool.

Tool Description gatekeeper_select_tool Translates a natural-language request into the most appropriate MCP tool call platform_get_capabilities Returns a help-style summary of all available API endpoints and tools platform_list_get_operations Lists all supported read-only GET operations and their input schemas platform_list_post_operations Lists all supported POST operations and their request body schemas profile_get_current_extension Returns the RingCentral extension for the authenticated bearer token

docs.title: Generic operations
docs.text:
Dynamic dispatch tools for calling any supported RingCentral Platform endpoint by operation name.

Tool Description platform_call_get_operation Executes any supported read-only RingCentral Platform GET operation platform_call_post_operation Executes any supported RingCentral Platform POST operation

docs.title: Team messaging
docs.text:
Tools for working with RingCentral Team Messaging (formerly Glip) chats, conversations, teams, and posts.

Tool Description platform_create_glip_conversation_new Create or open a direct or group conversation platform_create_glip_post_new Create a post in a chat platform_list_glip_chats_new List all chats the authenticated user belongs to platform_list_glip_conversations_new List direct and group conversations platform_list_glip_teams_new List teams the authenticated user is a member of platform_read_glip_conversation_new Get details about a specific conversation platform_read_glip_posts_new List posts in a chat platform_read_glip_team_new Get details about a specific team

docs.title: Messages
docs.text:
Tools for reading SMS, fax, voicemail, and pager messages from the message store.

Tool Description platform_list_messages List messages in a user's message store platform_read_message Get one or more messages by ID platform_read_message_content Download the binary content of a message attachment

docs.title: Call log
docs.text: Tool Description platform_read_user_call_log List call log records for a user's extension

docs.title: Extension & presence
docs.text: Tool Description platform_read_extension Get details about a RingCentral extension platform_read_unified_presence Get the unified presence status for an extension

docs.title: AI
docs.text: Tool Description platform_read_ai_notes Get AI-generated notes for a telephony session

docs.title: Directory
docs.text: Tool Description platform_search_directory_entries Search the company directory for extensions and users

docs.title: gatekeeper_select_tool
docs.text:
First stop for translating a natural-language RingCentral request into MCP tool calls. Selects one RingCentral MCP tool using endpoint input schemas.

Server: RingCentral MCP CRM required: No

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description userRequest string ✅ The natural-language request describing what the user wants to accomplish conversationContext string — Additional context from the ongoing conversation to improve tool selection intentHints string[] — Optional array of hint strings to help disambiguate the user's intent

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: Returns the name of the single most appropriate RingCentral MCP tool to call for the given request, along with any relevant metadata to guide the follow-up tool invocation.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Claude prompt 
I want to see my recent missed calls.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Use this tool as the entry point when a user's request is ambiguous and you are unsure which RingCentral MCP tool to invoke.
  • The tool examines all available endpoint input schemas to make its selection, so passing rich conversationContext improves accuracy.
  • After receiving the selected tool name, call that tool directly with the appropriate parameters.

Related tools

Follow up gatekeeper_select_tool with platform_get_capabilities if you need a broader overview of what operations are available before deciding.

docs.title: platform_call_get_operation
docs.text:
Executes a supported read-only RingCentral Platform GET operation. Missing accountId, extensionId, and ownerExtensionId path parameters default to ~.

Server: RingCentral MCP CRM required: No

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: This tool uses a dynamic dispatch model. The operation name and its parameters are not fixed — they are determined by the operations returned from platform_list_get_operations. Call that tool first to discover the valid operation identifiers and their expected input schemas, then pass the appropriate operation name and arguments to this tool.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: Returns the JSON response body from the underlying RingCentral Platform GET endpoint for the requested operation. The exact shape of the response depends on which operation is executed.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Claude prompt 
Show me the details for my RingCentral extension.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Always call platform_list_get_operations first to discover valid operation names and their schemas.
  • Path parameters accountId, extensionId, and ownerExtensionId default to ~, which resolves to the authenticated user's account and extension.
  • This tool covers read-only (GET) operations only. For write operations use platform_call_post_operation.

Related tools

Use platform_list_get_operations to browse available operations before calling this tool.

docs.title: platform_call_post_operation
docs.text:
Executes a supported RingCentral Platform POST operation with a JSON request body.

Server: RingCentral MCP CRM required: No

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: This tool uses a dynamic dispatch model. The operation name and its request body schema are not fixed — they are determined by the operations returned from platform_list_post_operations. Call that tool first to discover the valid operation identifiers and their expected input schemas, then pass the appropriate operation name and body to this tool.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: Returns the JSON response body from the underlying RingCentral Platform POST endpoint for the requested operation. The exact shape of the response depends on which operation is executed.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Claude prompt 
Search the company directory for everyone in the Engineering department.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Always call platform_list_post_operations first to discover valid operation names and their request body schemas.
  • Path parameters such as accountId default to ~, which resolves to the authenticated user's account.
  • This tool handles write and search (POST) operations. For read-only operations use platform_call_get_operation.

Related tools

Use platform_list_post_operations to browse available operations before calling this tool.

docs.title: platform_create_glip_conversation_new
docs.text:
Create or open a direct conversation (1:1 or group). Maps to the RingCentral REST API POST /team-messaging/v1/conversations.

Server: RingCentral MCP CRM required: No

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description body.members[].email string — Email address of a member to include in the conversation body.members[].id string — Extension ID of a member to include in the conversation

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: Returns the conversation object for the newly created or already-existing conversation, including its id, type, creation time, and member list.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Claude prompt 
Start a direct message conversation with alice@example.com.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• If a conversation with the exact same set of members already exists, the API returns the existing conversation rather than creating a duplicate.
  • Each member can be identified by either email or id; at least one of the two should be provided per member entry.
  • The authenticated user is automatically added as a member.

Related tools

After creating a conversation, use platform_create_glip_post_new to send the first message into it.

docs.title: platform_create_glip_post_new
docs.text:
Create a post in a RingCentral Team Messaging chat. Maps to the RingCentral REST API POST /team-messaging/v1/chats/{chatId}/posts.

Server: RingCentral MCP CRM required: No

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description path.chatId string ✅ ID of the chat to post into body.text string — Text content of the post body.attachments[].id string — ID of an attachment to include body.attachments[].type File \| Note \| Event \| Card — Type of the attachment

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: Returns the newly created post object, including its id, creationTime, lastModifiedTime, text, and any attachments.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Claude prompt 
Post "The weekly report is ready for review" to chat ID 62910238527.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Either body.text or at least one attachment must be supplied; a post cannot be empty.
  • Use platform_list_glip_chats_new or platform_list_glip_conversations_new to find a valid chatId before posting.
  • Attachment types File, Note, Event, and Card refer to RingCentral Team Messaging attachment objects, not local files.

Related tools

To read existing posts in a chat, use platform_read_glip_posts_new.

docs.title: platform_get_capabilities
docs.text:
Returns a help-style summary of the RingCentral API endpoints and MCP tools implemented by this service.

Server: RingCentral MCP CRM required: No

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: This tool takes no parameters.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: Returns a human-readable summary describing all RingCentral API endpoints and MCP tools available through this server, including brief descriptions of what each tool does and how to use it.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Claude prompt 
What can you do with the RingCentral MCP server?

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• This is the best starting point for discovering what is available on the server without calling individual list tools.
  • The response is intended to be read by an AI agent or surfaced directly to an end user as onboarding help.
  • For a machine-readable list of GET operations, use platform_list_get_operations; for POST operations use platform_list_post_operations.

Related tools

Use gatekeeper_select_tool after reviewing capabilities to route a specific user request to the right tool.

docs.title: platform_list_get_operations
docs.text:
Lists the supported read-only RingCentral Platform GET operations available through platform_call_get_operation.

Server: RingCentral MCP CRM required: No

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: This tool takes no parameters.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: Returns a list of all supported GET operation identifiers along with their input schemas, describing the path parameters, query parameters, and expected data types for each operation.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Claude prompt 
What read operations are available on the RingCentral platform?

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Call this tool before using platform_call_get_operation to ensure you are passing a valid operation name and correct parameters.
  • The returned schemas drive the dynamic dispatch in platform_call_get_operation.
  • For POST operations, use platform_list_post_operations instead.

Related tools

Pass one of the returned operation names to platform_call_get_operation to execute it.

docs.title: platform_list_glip_chats_new
docs.text:
List chats the authenticated user belongs to. Maps to the RingCentral REST API GET /team-messaging/v1/chats.

Server: RingCentral MCP CRM required: No

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description query.type Personal \| Direct \| Group \| Team \| Everyone — Filter by one or more chat types query.recordCount number — Maximum number of chats to return query.pageToken string — Pagination token from a previous response to retrieve the next page

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: Returns a paginated list of chat objects the authenticated user is a member of. Each entry includes the chat id, type, name (for teams and groups), creationTime, and member count.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Claude prompt 
Show me all the team chats I'm a member of.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Multiple values can be supplied for query.type to filter across several chat types at once.
  • Use the pageToken from the response to paginate through large result sets.
  • To list only conversations (1:1 and group DMs), use platform_list_glip_conversations_new; for teams only, use platform_list_glip_teams_new.

Related tools

Once you have a chatId, use platform_read_glip_posts_new to read its messages or platform_create_glip_post_new to post into it.

docs.title: platform_list_glip_conversations_new
docs.text:
List direct and group conversations for the authenticated user. Maps to the RingCentral REST API GET /team-messaging/v1/conversations.

Server: RingCentral MCP CRM required: No

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description query.recordCount number — Maximum number of conversations to return query.pageToken string — Pagination token from a previous response to retrieve the next page

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: Returns a paginated list of conversation objects (1:1 and group DMs) that the authenticated user participates in. Each entry includes the conversation id, type, member list, and creationTime.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Claude prompt 
List my recent direct message conversations.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• This endpoint returns only Direct and Group chat types. To include Teams and other types use platform_list_glip_chats_new.
  • Use the pageToken from the response to retrieve subsequent pages.
  • To open or create a new conversation, use platform_create_glip_conversation_new.

Related tools

Retrieve a specific conversation by ID with platform_read_glip_conversation_new.

docs.title: platform_list_glip_teams_new
docs.text:
List Team Messaging teams the authenticated user belongs to. Maps to the RingCentral REST API GET /team-messaging/v1/teams.

Server: RingCentral MCP CRM required: No

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description query.recordCount number — Maximum number of teams to return query.pageToken string — Pagination token from a previous response to retrieve the next page

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: Returns a paginated list of team objects the authenticated user is a member of. Each entry includes the team id, name, description, creationTime, and whether the team is public or private.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Claude prompt 
What RingCentral teams am I a member of?

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Only teams (type: Team) are returned; for direct and group conversations use platform_list_glip_conversations_new.
  • Use the pageToken from the response to paginate through large result sets.
  • To get details for a specific team by ID, use platform_read_glip_team_new.

Related tools

Once you have a team's chatId, post into it with platform_create_glip_post_new or read its posts with platform_read_glip_posts_new.

docs.title: platform_list_messages
docs.text:
List messages in a user's message store (SMS, fax, voicemail, pager). Maps to the RingCentral REST API GET /restapi/v1.0/account/{accountId}/extension/{extensionId}/message-store.

Server: RingCentral MCP CRM required: No

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description path.accountId string — Account ID; defaults to ~ (authenticated user's account) path.extensionId string — Extension ID; defaults to ~ (authenticated user's extension) query.messageType Fax \| SMS \| VoiceMail \| Pager — Filter by one or more message types query.direction Inbound \| Outbound — Filter by message direction query.readStatus Read \| Unread — Filter by read status query.dateFrom string — Start of date range in ISO 8601 format query.dateTo string — End of date range in ISO 8601 format query.conversationId string — Filter to a specific conversation thread query.phoneNumber string — Filter messages to or from a specific phone number query.distinctConversations boolean — Return only the most recent message per conversation query.page number — Page number for pagination query.perPage number — Number of records per page query.availability Alive \| Deleted \| Purged — Filter by message availability status query.owner Any \| Personal \| Shared or string[] — Filter by message ownership query.voicemailOwner string[] — Filter voicemails by owner extension ID(s) query.ownerExtensionType string — Filter by the extension type of the message owner

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: Returns a paginated list of message records from the user's message store. Each record includes message id, type, direction, readStatus, subject, sender and recipient details, and creationTime.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Claude prompt 
Show me all unread SMS messages from the past week.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• path.accountId and path.extensionId both default to ~, which resolves to the authenticated user's account and extension.
  • Multiple enum values can be supplied for messageType, direction, readStatus, and availability to broaden the filter.
  • To retrieve the content of a specific message, follow up with platform_read_message or platform_read_message_content.

Related tools

Retrieve a specific message by ID with platform_read_message, or download an attachment with platform_read_message_content.

docs.title: platform_list_post_operations
docs.text:
Lists the supported RingCentral Platform POST operations available through platform_call_post_operation.

Server: RingCentral MCP CRM required: No

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: This tool takes no parameters.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: Returns a list of all supported POST operation identifiers along with their request body schemas, describing the required and optional fields for each operation.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Claude prompt 
What write operations are supported on the RingCentral platform?

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Call this tool before using platform_call_post_operation to ensure you are passing a valid operation name and correct request body.
  • The returned schemas drive the dynamic dispatch in platform_call_post_operation.
  • For read-only GET operations, use platform_list_get_operations instead.

Related tools

Pass one of the returned operation names to platform_call_post_operation to execute it.

docs.title: platform_read_ai_notes
docs.text:
Get AI-generated notes for a telephony session. Maps to the RingCentral REST API GET /ai/copilot/v1/accounts/~/extensions/{ownerExtensionId}/ai-notes/{telephonySessionId}.

Server: RingCentral MCP CRM required: No

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description path.ownerExtensionId string ✅ Extension ID of the user who owns the AI notes path.telephonySessionId string ✅ Telephony session ID for which the AI notes were generated

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: Returns the AI-generated notes object for the specified telephony session, including the structured note content, summary, action items, and any key moments identified during the call.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Claude prompt 
Get the AI notes for my call session s-a0a00a00a00aa000a in extension 12345678.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• AI notes are generated by RingCentral's AI Copilot feature and are only available for calls where the feature was active.
  • The account path segment is always ~ and resolves to the authenticated user's account; it cannot be overridden.
  • Both ownerExtensionId and telephonySessionId are required — there is no default fallback for either parameter.

Related tools

Use platform_read_user_call_log to find telephonySessionId values from your recent call history.

docs.title: platform_read_extension
docs.text:
Get details about a RingCentral extension. Maps to the RingCentral REST API GET /restapi/v1.0/account/{accountId}/extension/{extensionId}.

Server: RingCentral MCP CRM required: No

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description path.accountId string — Account ID; defaults to ~ (authenticated user's account) path.extensionId string — Extension ID; defaults to ~ (authenticated user's extension)

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: Returns the extension object including the user's name, extension number, email, status, regional settings, and associated phone numbers.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Claude prompt 
What is my RingCentral extension number and email address?

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Both path.accountId and path.extensionId default to ~, so calling this tool with no parameters returns the authenticated user's own extension details.
  • To look up a different extension, supply the target extension's ID as path.extensionId.
  • For a higher-level view of the authenticated user (including token scope), consider profile_get_current_extension.

Related tools

Use platform_read_unified_presence to check the presence status of the same extension.

docs.title: platform_read_glip_conversation_new
docs.text:
Get details about a specific Team Messaging conversation. Maps to the RingCentral REST API GET /team-messaging/v1/conversations/{chatId}.

Server: RingCentral MCP CRM required: No

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description path.chatId string ✅ ID of the conversation to retrieve

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: Returns the conversation object including its id, type, member list with extension details, creationTime, and lastModifiedTime.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Claude prompt 
Get the details for conversation ID 62910238527.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Use platform_list_glip_conversations_new to discover conversation IDs before calling this tool.
  • This tool retrieves metadata about the conversation, not its messages. To read messages, use platform_read_glip_posts_new.
  • The authenticated user must be a member of the conversation to retrieve it.

Related tools

Read the messages in this conversation with platform_read_glip_posts_new, or post into it with platform_create_glip_post_new.

docs.title: platform_read_glip_posts_new
docs.text:
List posts in a Team Messaging chat. Maps to the RingCentral REST API GET /team-messaging/v1/chats/{chatId}/posts.

Server: RingCentral MCP CRM required: No

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description path.chatId string ✅ ID of the chat whose posts to retrieve query.recordCount number — Maximum number of posts to return query.pageToken string — Pagination token from a previous response to retrieve the next page

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: Returns a paginated list of post objects for the specified chat, ordered from most recent to oldest. Each post includes its id, text, creationTime, lastModifiedTime, creator information, and any attachments.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Claude prompt 
Show me the last 20 messages in chat 62910238527.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Use platform_list_glip_chats_new or platform_list_glip_conversations_new to find a valid chatId.
  • Posts are returned in reverse-chronological order by default; use pageToken to paginate backwards through history.
  • To send a new post to the chat, use platform_create_glip_post_new.

Related tools

Post a reply into this chat with platform_create_glip_post_new.

docs.title: platform_read_glip_team_new
docs.text:
Get details about a specific Team Messaging team. Maps to the RingCentral REST API GET /team-messaging/v1/teams/{chatId}.

Server: RingCentral MCP CRM required: No

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description path.chatId string ✅ ID of the team to retrieve

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: Returns the team object including its id, name, description, creationTime, lastModifiedTime, privacy setting (public or private), and member count.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Claude prompt 
Give me the details for team ID 62910238527.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Use platform_list_glip_teams_new to discover team IDs before calling this tool.
  • This tool returns team metadata only, not its posts. To read messages, use platform_read_glip_posts_new.
  • The authenticated user must be a member of the team to retrieve it.

Related tools

Read team messages with platform_read_glip_posts_new, or post into the team with platform_create_glip_post_new.

docs.title: platform_read_message_content
docs.text:
Get the binary content of a message attachment. Maps to the RingCentral REST API GET /restapi/v1.0/account/{accountId}/extension/{extensionId}/message-store/{messageId}/content/{attachmentId}.

Server: RingCentral MCP CRM required: No

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description path.accountId string — Account ID; defaults to ~ (authenticated user's account) path.extensionId string — Extension ID; defaults to ~ (authenticated user's extension) path.messageId string ✅ ID of the message containing the attachment path.attachmentId string ✅ ID of the specific attachment to download query.contentDisposition Inline \| Attachment — Controls whether the content is rendered inline or downloaded as a file query.contentDispositionFilename string — Filename hint to use when the content is served as a download

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: Returns the raw binary content of the specified attachment (e.g. a fax image, voicemail audio file, or MMS media file) along with the appropriate Content-Type header.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Claude prompt 
Download the fax attachment with ID 111222333 from message 9876543210.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• path.accountId and path.extensionId both default to ~, which resolves to the authenticated user's account and extension.
  • Attachment IDs can be found in the attachments array of a message object returned by platform_read_message.
  • Use query.contentDisposition: Attachment combined with query.contentDispositionFilename to prompt a file download in browser-based contexts.

Related tools

First retrieve the message and its attachment IDs with platform_read_message.

docs.title: platform_read_message
docs.text:
Get one or more messages from a user's message store. Maps to the RingCentral REST API GET /restapi/v1.0/account/{accountId}/extension/{extensionId}/message-store/{messageId}.

Server: RingCentral MCP CRM required: No

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description path.accountId string — Account ID; defaults to ~ (authenticated user's account) path.extensionId string — Extension ID; defaults to ~ (authenticated user's extension) path.messageId string[] ✅ One or more message IDs to retrieve

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: Returns the message object(s) for the specified ID(s), including message type, direction, readStatus, subject, sender and recipient details, creationTime, and a list of attachment references.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Claude prompt 
Get the details for message IDs 1234567890 and 9876543210.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• path.accountId and path.extensionId both default to ~, which resolves to the authenticated user's account and extension.
  • Multiple message IDs can be passed in a single call by providing an array of strings to path.messageId.
  • To download the binary content of an attachment referenced in a message, use platform_read_message_content.

Related tools

Find message IDs first with platform_list_messages, then download attachments with platform_read_message_content.

docs.title: platform_read_unified_presence
docs.text:
Get the unified presence status for a RingCentral extension. Maps to the RingCentral REST API GET /restapi/v1.0/account/{accountId}/extension/{extensionId}/unified-presence.

Server: RingCentral MCP CRM required: No

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description path.accountId string — Account ID; defaults to ~ (authenticated user's account) path.extensionId string — Extension ID; defaults to ~ (authenticated user's extension)

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: Returns the unified presence object for the specified extension, including the aggregated presence status (e.g. Available, Busy, DoNotDisturb), telephony session presence, meeting presence, and glip (Team Messaging) presence.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Claude prompt 
What is my current presence status on RingCentral?

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Both path.accountId and path.extensionId default to ~, so calling this tool with no parameters returns the authenticated user's own presence.
  • The unified presence aggregates status across telephony, meetings, and Team Messaging into a single top-level status.
  • To look up the extension profile rather than its presence, use platform_read_extension.

Related tools

Use platform_read_extension to retrieve the full extension profile alongside presence information.

docs.title: platform_read_user_call_log
docs.text:
List call log records for a user's extension. Maps to the RingCentral REST API GET /restapi/v1.0/account/{accountId}/extension/{extensionId}/call-log.

Server: RingCentral MCP CRM required: No

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description path.accountId string — Account ID; defaults to ~ (authenticated user's account) path.extensionId string — Extension ID; defaults to ~ (authenticated user's extension) query.direction Inbound \| Outbound — Filter by call direction query.type Voice \| Fax — Filter by call type query.dateFrom string — Start of date range in ISO 8601 format query.dateTo string — End of date range in ISO 8601 format query.view Simple \| Detailed — Level of detail in the response (Detailed includes per-leg data) query.withRecording boolean — Return only calls that have a recording query.recordingType Automatic \| OnDemand \| All — Filter by recording type query.phoneNumber string — Filter calls to or from a specific phone number query.extensionNumber string — Filter calls to or from a specific extension number query.sessionId string — Filter to a specific call session query.telephonySessionId string — Filter to a specific telephony session query.transport PSTN \| VoIP — Filter by call transport type query.showBlocked boolean — Include calls from blocked numbers query.showDeleted boolean — Include deleted call log records query.metadataCategory string[] — Filter by metadata category query.page number — Page number for pagination query.perPage number — Number of records per page

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: Returns a paginated list of call log records for the specified extension. Each record includes call id, direction, type, startTime, duration, caller/callee details, telephony session IDs, and recording references if applicable.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Claude prompt 
Show me all inbound calls I received in the last 7 days that were recorded.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• path.accountId and path.extensionId both default to ~, so calling this tool with no path parameters returns the authenticated user's own call log.
  • Use query.view: Detailed to retrieve per-leg data for multi-party or transferred calls.
  • The telephonySessionId in each record can be used with platform_read_ai_notes to retrieve AI-generated call notes.

Related tools

Use telephonySessionId values from call log records to fetch AI notes with platform_read_ai_notes.

docs.title: platform_search_directory_entries
docs.text:
Search the company directory for extensions, users, and contacts. Maps to the RingCentral REST API POST /restapi/v1.0/account/{accountId}/directory/entries/search.

Server: RingCentral MCP CRM required: No

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description path.accountId string — Account ID; defaults to ~ (authenticated user's account) body.searchString string — Free-text search string to match against directory entries body.searchFields firstName \| lastName \| extensionNumber \| phoneNumber \| email \| jobTitle \| department \| customFieldValue — Fields to search within; multiple values allowed body.extensionTypes string — Filter by extension type (e.g. User, Department, Voicemail) body.extensionStatuses Enabled \| Disabled \| NotActivated — Filter by extension status; multiple values allowed body.extensionIds string[] — Limit results to specific extension IDs body.accountIds string[] — Limit results to specific account IDs (for federated directories) body.siteIds string[] — Limit results to specific site IDs body.department string — Filter by department name body.showFederated boolean — Include entries from federated (partner) accounts body.showExternalContacts boolean — Include external contacts in the results body.showAdminOnlyContacts boolean — Include contacts visible only to administrators body.page number — Page number for pagination body.perPage number — Number of records per page body.orderBy[].fieldName firstName \| lastName \| extensionNumber \| phoneNumber \| email \| jobTitle \| department — Field to sort results by body.orderBy[].direction Asc \| Desc — Sort direction for the corresponding fieldName

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: Returns a paginated list of directory entry objects matching the search criteria. Each entry includes the user's name, extension number, email, department, job title, phone numbers, and extension type.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Claude prompt 
Find all enabled users in the Engineering department and sort them by last name.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• path.accountId defaults to ~, which resolves to the authenticated user's account.
  • Multiple values can be supplied for body.searchFields, body.extensionStatuses, and body.extensionTypes to broaden or refine the search.
  • The body.orderBy array supports multi-level sorting: add multiple objects with different fieldName values to sort by primary and secondary fields.

Related tools

Once you have an extension ID from the directory, retrieve its full profile with platform_read_extension or check its presence with platform_read_unified_presence.

docs.title: profile_get_current_extension
docs.text:
Returns the RingCentral extension for the authenticated bearer token. This tool always returns the caller's own extension and cannot query arbitrary account or extension IDs.

Server: RingCentral MCP CRM required: No

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: This tool takes no parameters.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: Returns the extension object associated with the current bearer token, including the user's name, extension number, email address, account ID, and status. This is effectively the "who am I" endpoint for the authenticated session.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Claude prompt 
Who am I logged in as on RingCentral?

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• This tool is scoped strictly to the authenticated user; it cannot be used to look up other extensions.
  • Use this as a reliable way to retrieve the current user's extensionId and accountId before passing ~ is insufficient.
  • For richer extension details (regional settings, phone numbers, etc.), follow up with platform_read_extension.

Related tools

Use platform_read_extension for a more detailed extension profile, or platform_read_unified_presence to check your current presence status.
